title: TNO Image Fusion Dataset
abstract: The TNO Image Fusion Dataset contains nultispectral (intensified visual, near-infrared, and longwave infrared or thermal) nighttime imagery of different military relevant scenerios, registered with different multiband camnera systems. The different camera systems used to register this imagery are respectively Athena, DHV, FEL, and TRICLOBS. Imagery recorded with these systems are stored in folders labeled with the corresponding camera system name. Information on the registration conditions and the respective camera systems is included in the REFRENCES sections in each of the folders. The images can freely be used for research purposes, and may be used in publications without prior notice, provided proper credit is given to the owner (TNO, Soesterberg, The Netherlands) and this figshare dataset is properly referenced.

narrative:
Short impact summary

The TNO Image Fusion Dataset shows clear scholarly uptake as a reusable reference resource for multimodal image fusion: it has 202 citations in OpenAlex and 216 documented downstream reuses, alongside 39 recorded downloads and 112 views. Its influence is concentrated in technical STEM venues, especially infrared imaging, image fusion, and computer vision research.

Full narrative

Released in 2014 on Figshare, the TNO Image Fusion Dataset has become an established infrastructure dataset for researchers working on multispectral and nighttime imagery. The citation record points to sustained use over time, with uptake appearing early and then broadening substantially in later years, including a strong rise in the 2021–2025 period. The dataset is openly accessible and has a clear version history in the repository record.

The reuse profile indicates that the dataset functions as a reference backbone for method development rather than as a one-off example. Most documented reuse appears in journal articles, with additional use in conference papers and preprints. The citing landscape is anchored in journals such as Infrared Physics & Technology, Information Fusion, IEEE Access, and IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement, which is consistent with the dataset’s technical role in image fusion and related computer vision workflows.

The topical focus of reuse is also tightly aligned with the dataset’s design. The strongest concepts in the citing record cluster around advanced image fusion techniques, image enhancement, infrared target detection, and remote-sensing image classification. Recent citing works in 2025 continue this pattern, including papers on infrared-visible fusion architectures, attention mechanisms, and transformer-based approaches. This suggests that the dataset remains relevant for contemporary algorithm development as well as for benchmarking.

The public-facing usage signals are modest compared with the citation record: the dataset has 39 downloads and 112 views in the available records, and no event-data mentions are available. Teaching adoption evidence is limited to a WorldCat holdings signal, so the record supports reuse and research uptake more strongly than classroom use. Overall, the dataset’s impact is best understood as durable scholarly infrastructure for infrared and multimodal image fusion research.
